subject: Shiny Server with nginx proxy_pass issue with trailing slashes

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Shiny Server with nginx proxy_pass issue with trailing slashes
parts:
I was playing with these instructions for setting up a Shiny Server with nginx, and I've encountered something odd that is probably the result of my total newness to nginx and server configuration generally.

Everything works fine, except the URLs for my Shiny apps can't have trailing slashes. You can see the behavior I'm talking about by looking at one of Dean's (the author of the instructions) shiny apps:

http://daattali.com/shiny/shinyjs-demo/

Using that URL works fine, but if you drop the trailing slash, nginx appears to redirect immediately to http://daattali.com/shinyjs-demo, dropping the /shiny/ part.

I'm seeing the exact same behavior with my apps.

My shiny server configuration is just the default with:

location / {

  site_dir /srv/shiny-server;

  log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

  directory_index on;

}

And I edited the nginx configuration to include:

location /shiny/ {

  proxy_pass http://123.456.789.000:3838/;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";

}

Does anyone know what shiny server/nginx configuration needs to be tweaked so that, e.g. in Dean's example above both

http://daattali.com/shiny/shinyjs-demo/ and
http://daattali.com/shiny/shinyjs-demo

will land at the same place?

- Joran

messages.author: 6a8c80c3e37f4389
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server with nginx proxy_pass issue with trailing slashes
parts:
Did you find any solution to this? I'm having the exact same problem, but on Apache.

Interestingly, the dropping out of the URL only occurs when the shiny app specified DOES exist, otherwise it's fine (though it won't find an app obviously). Very strange, but makes me think Shiny Server must be doing this somehow.

messages.author: 6a8c80c3e37f4389
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server with nginx proxy_pass issue with trailing slashes
parts:
Ah nevermind! The fix I was using is sufficient after all, it was just my browser storing old behaviours.

This is what I added to my VirtualHost:

  RewriteEngine on
  RewriteRule ^/shiny$ /shiny/ [R]
  RewriteRule ^(/shiny/[^/]+)$ $1/ [R]
